key_insight: Discrete diffusion models can have an analogue of the probability flow ODE used in continuous diffusion. The paper introduces exponential residual flows (ERFs), augmenting discrete states with continuous residual variables to enable this formulation.
problem_solved: Continuous diffusion has a deterministic ODE formulation that supports accelerated sampling and consistency distillation. This work addresses whether an analogous formulation exists for discrete diffusion models.
method: Introduce exponential residual flows as an ODE-based framework for discrete diffusion.
Augment each discrete state with a continuous residual variable.
Use the augmented representation to construct a discrete counterpart of probability flow dynamics.
impact: The framework provides a foundation for exploring accelerated sampling and consistency distillation in discrete diffusion models. The supplied abstract is truncated and does not establish specific speedups or benchmark gains.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: continuous diffusion and probability flow ODE versus discrete diffusion and ERFs.

Trajectory sketch showing continuous residual evolution alongside changes in discrete state.
Application icons highlighting potential faster sampling and consistency distillation.
paper_title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Samson Gourevitch, Yazid Janati, Eric Moulines, Eric P. Xing, Alain Durmus
